source_text: Ἔτι δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς καὶ περὶ τῶν ἰδίων ἐπιστολῶν (verba Eusebii sunt in lib. iv. Hist. c. 23.) ὡς ῥᾳδιουργηθεισῶν, ταῦτα φησίν. Ἐπιστολὰς γὰρ ἀδελφῶν ἀξιωσάντων με γράψαι, ἔνραψα. καὶ ταύτας οἱ τοῦ διαβόλου ἀπόστολοι ζιζανίων γεγέμικαν· ἃ μὲν ἐξαιροῦντες, ἃ δὲ προστιθέντες· οἷς τὸ οὐαὶ κεῖται. οὐ θαυμαστὸν ἄρα εἰ καὶ τῶν Κυριακῶν ῥαδιουργῆσαί τινες (for. legend. τινας) ἐπιβέβληνται γραφῶν, ὁπότε καὶ ταῖς οὐ τοιαύταις ἐπιβεβλήκασι (alii ἐπιβουλεύκασι).
thought_title: The devil's agents have corrupted my letters
orientation: Dionysius is speaking in his own voice, quoted by Eusebius, about what happened to his own letters.
pass_a_gloss: And further the same man also concerning his own letters (the words are Eusebius's in book 4 of the History, chapter 23) as having been tampered with, says these things. For when brothers asked me to write letters, I wrote them. And these the agents of the devil have filled with weeds: some things taking out, other things adding; for whom the woe is laid up. It is not wonderful therefore if some have undertaken to tamper even with the Lord's writings, when they have laid hands even on those not such.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'weeds' for ζιζάνια, used of corruptions inserted into the letters.
Glossary requires 'agents of the devil' for ἀπόστολοι τοῦ διαβόλου.
The brief notes 'the Lord's writings' (αἱ Κυριακαὶ γραφαί) as Dionysius's phrase for Scripture; literal rendering preserves the possessive.

choices.english: for whom the woe is laid up
choices.why: Literal rendering of the dative of disadvantage and the verb κεῖται, preserving the threat's passive force.
The variant reading in the apparatus (ἐπιβουλεύκασι would be 'have plotted against'); the main reading ἐπιβεβλήκασι means 'have laid hands on' or 'have set upon', fitting the context of tampering.

pass_b_english: Dionysius also says this about his own letters, namely that they were tampered with. "When the brethren asked me to write letters, I wrote them. And the agents of the devil have filled these with weeds, taking some things out and adding others. For them the woe is laid up. It is no wonder, then, that some have undertaken to tamper even with the Lord's writings, when they have laid hands on writings that are not such as these."
notes: The source text contains a parenthetical note in Latin: '(verba Eusebii sunt in lib. iv. Hist. c. 23.)' indicating these are Eusebius's words in book 4, chapter 23 of the History.
The text has a marginal note '(for. legend. τινας)' suggesting the reading τινας instead of τινες after ῥᾳδιουργῆσαι.
The text has a variant note '(alii ἐπιβουλεύκασι)' indicating some manuscripts read ἐπιβουλεύκασι instead of ἐπιβεβλήκασι.
